newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister upholds B Band disqualifications.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister upholds B Band disqualifications.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta upheld Thursday the disqualifications of five consortia from bidding for multi-billion-dollar cellular telephone concessions.

The groups, which were disqualified in June by a ministry committee, may now appeal against their disqualification from the B Band bidding in the courts, a ministry spokesman said. The five disqualifed groups were:
-- Consorcio Hutchison/Cowan, comprising Hong Kong communications group Hutchison Whampoa and Brazilian construction company Cowan Construtora;
-- MCom Wireless, including investment bank Banco Garantia, Mexico's Telmex and Comcast ;
-- Lightel, made up of private communications group Lightel, construction firm Queiroz Galvao and Korean Mobile Telecom;
-- Algar, with the same members as Lightel;
-- Tess, including Sweden's Telia and Airline Cellular and construction company CR Almeida, both of Brazil.
Motta also disqualified another group, Telet, from bidding for contracts in three of Brazil's most lucrative regions: Sao Paulo city, Sao Paulo state and Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states.
Telet includes BCE Inc's Bell Canada and Telesystem of Montreal, Citibank and Brazilian pension funds.
On Wednesday, the Americel group, which includes the same members as Telet, signed a first B Band contract to provide cellular services in a region of Brazil's centerwest.

Motta has said he intends to open July 9 price bids from groups seeking to win the Sao Paulo city concession, considered the biggest prize of the B Band program, and another concession to provide services in the states of Bahia and Sergipe.

A total of ten regional concessions are on offer in the first stage of the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry. The government hopes to raise about $6.0 billion with the sale of license fees.
